json.summary: Ilya spoke with Jane Cooper and Wade Warren at Northwind about monitoring their autonomous warehouse robots. Northwind described a patchwork of logs and a slow dashboard, costly manual support visits and a key customer renewal tied to uptime. They agreed to run a pilot on one site, schedule a technical deep dive and review a short proposal by Friday.
json.concise_summary: Northwind: fleet monitoring gaps and uptime pressure. Pilot on one site, deep dive next week, proposal by Fri.

sections.content: The team wants dependable, real-time visibility into the robot fleet and fewer unplanned site visits.
items: Improve fleet visibility with real-time telemetry across deployed robots.
Reduce on-site visits and downtime ahead of the customer renewal.
Detect issues earlier instead of waiting for a robot to stop.

sections.content: Monitoring is a patchwork of logs and a dashboard that refreshes every fifteen minutes.
items: Current monitoring is a patchwork that the team does not trust.
When a robot fails, support pulls logs manually and sends a technician.
Unplanned site visits are costly and some contracts include uptime penalties.

sections.content: They run their own log server and a dashboard for battery level and error codes.
items: Each robot pushes logs to Northwind's own server.
A dashboard shows battery level and error codes but refreshes slowly.
Support relies on calls and manual log review.

sections.content: A pilot is possible within the contact's own approval limit; larger amounts need the CFO.
items: Budget up to the contact's approval limit, above that the CFO decides.
Pilot target: fewer site visits by the end of the quarter.

sections.content: Set up a technical deep dive and send a short pilot proposal.
items: Set up a technical deep dive with the head of engineering next week.
Send a short pilot proposal by Friday.
Pilot the solution on one site and review results at the end of the quarter.
